items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...who was it that Saeed's brother-in-law or something? Oh, Benny Benoit. [INTERVIEWEE] I was playing with him with the Liberty Band...

ctx.x: Well, after the Navy, they was not making a reserve Navy band. I got in the inactive reserve and when the Army was making a band at Spencer, a very good bass player, teaching music in New Iberraighton, I think. Well, he told me, he said, I'm gonna get an Army band here in the band again. He said, with your rating, he said, you'll be way up there. So I said, I think I will. So I got in the Navy, an Army band then, and Army, Melvin C. Bryant, a music teacher at Dillard University, had a charge in the band. Well, I…
Well, you mentioned outside some, who was it that Saeed's brother-in-law or something? Oh, Benny Benoit.

I was playing with him with the Liberty Band, but I gnawly passed. That's years ago. I remember when I gnawly passed and myself, we were playing at the Crystal Palace in Depression time up on Clio and Radha, near Drys. And all the boys from Browns, the ice cream company used to come there, you know. And I know I told him, son, you don't drink now. I said, no, son. He said, well, don't turn no beer on.
